tests_added_or_updated: 24 new independent adversarial tests in one new file (tests/test_cltr_migration_135p_verification.py) covering entry-point recovery-classification wiring, non-authority-disclosure cross-module consistency, transition-ID collision resistance at scale, unreachable/undisclosed comparison classes, comparison-class field coverage, persistence crash-mid-sequence, commit-ownership type-mismatch containment, and all four production entry points driven through the real finalization boundary end-to-end
summary: Phase 135P independently re-derived and adversarially verified Phase 135O's Stage 1 shared transition-input and dual-derivation implementation against CLTR-001, CLTR-SCHEMA-001 v1.0.1, and the verified 135M/135N migration contract -- not against 135O's own report or docstrings. All 13 modules under src/pcae/cltr/migration/ were independently read in full, along with the shared finalization boundary (src/pcae/core/finalization_transaction.py), all four production entry-point call sites (task.py, phase.py, phase_reports.py, notifications.py), and all 77 pre-existing migration tests. 24 new adversarial tests were written and executed against real production code paths, including the first test in the repository to drive all four entry points (task_finish, phase_complete, phase_report_create, notify_send_report) through the real run_finalization_transaction() boundary end-to-end and read back persisted evidence. Zero Blocking defects were found or reproduced: legacy lifecycle authority is preserved everywhere; design-B transition_id is genuinely non-derivable from title, Git, or repository HEAD; deep immutability holds under nested-mutation, alias-mutation, and post-digest-mutation attack; comparison classification is deterministic; migration evidence is truthfully bound to a single shared input revision; filesystem containment holds under path-traversal and symlink attack; persistence crash-mid-sequence leaves prior evidence untouched and never claims partial completion as success; and no subprocess, socket, shell, or backend-invocation capability exists anywhere in the migration package. Four new Non-Blocking findings were independently discovered: F-135P-1 (two of four entry points fall back to a generic recovery classification instead of their dedicated one -- proven inert for comparison and progression eligibility); F-135P-2 (temporal_order_mismatch/expected_representation_difference are declared comparison-class wire identifiers with no field-comparison logic capable of ever producing them, undisclosed as such); F-135P-3 (derive_cltr would crash with AttributeError on non-empty phase_commit_ownership since raw commit-hash strings are forwarded into a field typed tuple[CommitOwnershipEntry, ...] -- dormant today because the sole production call site hardcodes an empty tuple, fully contained by complete()'s outer exception handler); F-135P-4 (the non-authority disclosure dict is independently hardcoded five times with no shared source of truth). No production source file under src/ was modified; all findings are locked in by new regression tests rather than silently repaired outside this phase's narrow Blocking-only repair boundary. All five 135N/135L/135J inherited Non-Blocking findings were independently re-evaluated and correctly remain open, out of this phase's implementation-verification scope. 101/101 combined migration tests pass (77 existing + 24 new); 386/386 combined CLTR tests pass; 117/117 affected finalization regressions pass; 4391/4391 Fast Green, unchanged from pre-phase baseline. No Stage 2 implementation, atomic authoritative publication, authority cutover, or legacy-authority demotion/retirement occurred. Recommends 135Q - Atomic Publication Rehearsal Contract and Implementation Plan (architecture/contract/planning only).
